term: A10 rule-of-thumb causal default and prima-facie expectation
definition: A10P1’s rule-of-thumb title gives a defeasible reason to expect a property of a particular encountered class member, allowing counter-reasons that mark it as an exception. Applied to contingency and causation, its question asks whether contingent things generally have causes. Cause means a prior condition capable of explaining or partly explaining an event/change. The title’s every-A-is-B wording describes the general default, not an exceptionless theorem once exceptions are explicitly allowed.
note: The source’s particle worry and size/shape/parts questions are examples of proposed exceptions or distinctions, not established quantum facts, causal invariance laws or metaphysically possible models. A possible beginning partless angel is a route-specific question, not a universal background. No actual statistical sample or complete exception set is supplied. Transfer to a selected first contingent in a possible history, evidence aggregation and defeater resolution remain OPEN. No probability measure, numeric bound, actual concrete support, universal PSR, asymmetry, transitivity or well-foundedness follows from this gloss. The weak prior partial-explanation sense differs from a complete existential ground and from the stronger temporal-presence/absence guards of existing count/history results; applicability to all contingents and serious brute/nonnecessitating/holistic rivals remains OPEN. A10P3C specifically reasks this defeasible default under the revised automatic-existence classification; it supplies no exceptionless revised-contingents-caused premise. Bounded analyst exploration: TruthCore.Causality.A10PreferentialExpectation.Profile/Expect uses arbitrary epistemic interpretation, evidence and case carriers; observation compatibility, undominated interpretations, observed positive support, explicit case applicability, no observed defeater, nonempty best class and unanimous best-case cause reports. This is a preferential candidate, NOT the original sourced sense binding or a numerical probability model. Preference and evidence calibration remain OPEN. A possible example is an encountered contingent with positive causal traces; a counterexample is a case outside that trace reference class or with defeating evidence. These examples are methodological, not established physical claims. Updating observations can withdraw expectation. Epistemic cause reports have no transitivity, asymmetry or objective existence laws. The generic possibleFromBridge requires an independent same-case accessible-world realization bridge. scenarioFromBridge carries no A10 content: its bridge consequent PossiblyExternallyCausedAt mentions neither the interpretation nor the case, and its concrete totality cause exists at an accessible history, not the actual world, so it only rewraps the existing Scenario antecedent. The same-case candidate sameCaseNecessarySource adds an OPEN analyst dictionary src from interpretation and case to Scenario bearer and a SameCaseBridge requiring that named bearer to be a guarded (beginning, existing concrete, outside-all-contingents) totality cause in an accessible history; with UniversalFrame the selected best interpretation's named cause is an actual necessary concretum. Prior partial explanation alone supplies none of these guards. Brute-only and mixed Scenario fixtures witness bridge omission, same-case nonvacuity, dictionary load-bearing (old bridge holds, same-case conclusion fails) and expectation load-bearing. These are finite formal controls, not metaphysical possibility certificates. Original declaration/allowance stays unresolved: no supplied source policy fixes observations, preference, reference class or defeaters, and selected-first-contingent applicability and prior-partial-cause-to-totality transport remain unproved. See explorations/necessarybeing-a10-preferential-expectation.toml.
